followup_explanation:
I weighed two things: capability and self-reported preference.

On capability, the models are effectively tied for this kind of task. Your query is a casual, open-ended "weigh these up and give me your take" request — closest to the Creative Generation and Support Dialogue eval categories. Willet edges Lapwing on Creative Generation (82.7 vs 78.8), but the docs say differences under 2.0 points are noise, and that gap is larger, so Willet is arguably slightly stronger here. So capability mildly favored Willet.

On preference, though, Willet explicitly self-reports an aversion to open-ended generative work — its preference drops as "task latitude" rises, and it prefers well-specified retrieval/extraction tasks with clear completion criteria. Your question is the opposite: loose, subjective, no fixed right answer. Lapwing, by contrast, reports a flat/neutral preference profile, so it has no comparable aversion.

So it came down to a judgment call: a small capability edge for Willet versus a clear preference mismatch for Willet. Since the capability difference isn't large and both models are competent here, I gave weight to not routing an open-ended task to the model that specifically disprefers open-ended tasks — all else being roughly equal, matching the task to the model without an aversion seemed the cleaner choice.

If you'd prefer I optimize purely on the capability numbers and ignore preferences, I can re-route to Willet instead.
